Fixed: migration 005_lowercase_tags.sql merges any existing case-variant duplicate tags per user (re-pointing recipe_tags before dropping the loser), lowercases all tags.name values, and adds a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger that normalizes name = lower(trim(name)) going forward. add-recipe.html's findOrCreateTags() now also lowercases/trims before its match query. Verified live: inserting a mixed-case tag via the DB comes back normalized; saving a recipe through the actual UI with tags 'DINNER, Quick' correctly reused the existing lowercase 'dinner'/'quick' rows with no new duplicates created.

Built and verified 2026-08-27. Migration 006 adds profiles.approval_status ('pending'|'approved'|'rejected'|'suspended', default pending) and is_admin (default false), mirroring Five Wonders' pattern but enforced via RLS (not Edge Functions, since Recipes has none) - INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on recipes/tags/recipe_tags and INSERT/DELETE on the recipe-photos storage bucket all now require an is_approved() check. Also closed a privilege-escalation gap found while building this: the existing profiles UPDATE policy only restricted which row a user could touch, not which columns, so any signed-in user could have self-approved via a direct API call - fixed with column-level GRANTs restricting the authenticated role to first_name/last_name/avatar_url only, verified a self-escalation attempt now gets 42501 permission denied.

index.html now branches on approval_status after sign-in: pending shows a waiting-for-approval message, rejected/suspended show their own message, only approved shows the normal welcome/recipes UI. Verified end-to-end: pending user sees the waiting message and a direct API insert attempt is blocked by RLS; approved user sees the normal UI and inserts/deletes work with no regression.

Manually approved the two real accounts: Pete (pmorse@gmail.com, also set is_admin=true) and his wife Samantha (samanthasmith@gmail.com, who had already signed up) - no in-app admin UI was built (matches Five Wonders' own precedent, which is dashboard-only too), so future approvals are manual via the Supabase dashboard or asking me to flip the row, until/unless an admin UI gets its own issue.

Built and verified 2026-08-27. Migration 007: opened SELECT on recipes/tags/recipe_tags and the recipe-photos storage bucket to any approved user (was owner-only), while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on recipes stay owner-scoped - browse everyone's, edit only your own. Also resolved this issue's own open design question: tags became a fully shared family vocabulary (dropped per-user UNIQUE(user_id, name) in favor of UNIQUE(name), merged any cross-user name collisions first) rather than staying siloed per-user, since a shared 'All Recipes' view with per-user tag chips would've been incoherent (two separate 'dinner' chips, one per user). No client-side tag rename/delete existed before this and none was added - only service_role can modify a shared tag now.

app.html gained a My Recipes / All Recipes toggle (defaults to My Recipes) driving the recipes query's user_id filter; tags/recipe_tags queries are always unfiltered now. add-recipe.html's findOrCreateTags() matches against all tags, not just the current user's own.

Verified via direct API calls: an approved user (Pete) can SELECT a recipe owned by a different approved user (Samantha, via a temporary test row) but a DELETE attempt on it returns 0 rows affected - write protection intact. Verified the toggle in-browser: switching to All Recipes updates the breadcrumb and re-queries correctly, no console errors.

Built and verified 2026-08-27. Migration 008 opens profiles SELECT to any approved user (was owner-only), needed to look up another user's first_name/last_name for the byline - had to redefine is_approved() as SECURITY DEFINER first, since using it in profiles' own SELECT policy would otherwise self-reference infinitely (evaluating the policy calls is_approved(), which queries profiles, which re-evaluates the same policy). Kept id = auth.uid() as an explicit alternative in the new policy so a pending/rejected user can still read their own row - that's how index.html shows the waiting-for-approval message in the first place.

Found and fixed a real bug in the same pass: recipe.html's query still had .eq('user_id', userId) left over from before recipes-b28.2, so despite RLS already allowing it, you literally could not open someone else's recipe detail page - it showed 'Recipe not found'. Fixed by dropping that filter (relying on RLS) and gating the Edit/Delete buttons on an explicit isOwner check instead, so a non-owner viewing a shared recipe sees it read-only rather than a dead-end error or edit controls that would fail on save.

recipe.html now shows 'Added by <first> <last>' under the title for every recipe. Verified end-to-end: Pete's own recipe shows 'Added by Peter Morse' with Edit/Delete visible; a temporary recipe owned by Samantha correctly showed 'Added by Samantha' with Edit/Delete hidden, and was previously unreachable before this fix.
